source_text:
quam uero unitatem seruat, quam dilectionem custodit aut cogitat qui discordiae furore uesanus ecclesiam scindit, fidem destruit, pacem turbat, caritatem dissipat, sacramentum profanat P
Malum. hoc, fidelissimi fratres, iam pridem coeperat, sed nunc creuit eiusdem mali infesta clades et surgere ac pullulare plus coepit haereticae peruersitatis et schismatum uenenata pernicies, quia et sic in occasu mundi oportebat praenuntiante per apostolum nobis et praemonente Spiritu sancto: in nouissimis, inquit, diebus aderunt tempora molesta, erunt homines sibi placentes, superbi, tumidi, cupidi, blasphemi. parentibus in dicto non audientes, ingrati, impii, sine adfectu, sine foedere, delatores, incontinentes, inmites, bonum non amantes, proditores, procaces, stupore inflati, uoluptates magis quam Deum diligentes, habentes deformationem religionis, uirtutem autem eius abnegantes. ex his sunt qui repunt in domos et praedantur mulierculas oneratas peccatis quae ducuntur uariis desideriis, semper discentes et numquam ad scientiam ueritatis peruenientes. et quomodo Iannes et Mambres restiterunt Moysi, sic et hi resistunt ueritati, sed non proficient plurimum. imperitia enim eorum manifesta erit omnibus, sicut et illorum fuit. adimplentur quaecumque praedicta sunt et adpropinquante iam saeculi fine hominum pariter ac temporum probatione uenerunt. magis ac magis aduersario saeuiente error fallit, extollit stupor, liuor incendit, cupiditas excaecat, deprauat inpietas, superbia inflat, discordia exasperat, ira praecipitat.
thought_title: The growth of schism and heresy in the last days
orientation: Cyprian is addressing the faithful about those who break the Church's unity, and now describes how this evil has grown as the end of the world approaches.
pass_a_gloss: But what unity does he keep, what love does he guard or think about, who, mad with the fury of discord, splits the Church, destroys faith, disturbs peace, scatters love, profanes the sacred sign? This evil, most faithful brothers, had begun already long ago, but now the hostile disaster of the same evil has grown, and the poisoned ruin of heretical perversity and of schisms has begun to rise up and sprout more and more, because it was necessary that it be so at the setting of the world, with the Holy Spirit foretelling through the apostle and warning us beforehand: in the last days, he says, troublesome times will be present; there will be men pleasing themselves, proud, puffed up, covetous, blasphemers, not listening to parents in a word, ungrateful, impious, without affection, without covenant, accusers, incontinent, ungentle, not loving good, traitors, reckless, swollen with stupor, loving pleasures more than God, having a form of religion but denying its power. From these are those who creep into houses and prey upon little women loaded with sins, who are led by various desires, always learning and never arriving at knowledge of the truth. And just as Jannes and Jambres resisted Moses, so also these resist the truth, but they will not get very far. For their ignorance will be evident to all, just as theirs also was. Whatever things have been foretold are being fulfilled, and with the end of the age now drawing near, the testing of men and of times alike has come. With the adversary raging more and more, error deceives, stupor puffs up, envy inflames, greed blinds, impiety corrupts, pride swells, discord embitters, anger hurls headlong.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'sacred sign' for sacramentum, which here refers to the sacred mystery of the Church's unity that the schismatic profanes.
The glossary requires 'love' for caritas, not 'charity', to convey the bond of love among the faithful that the schismatic scatters.
The glossary requires 'Church' for ecclesia, not 'assembly' or 'congregation', to keep the theological sense of the one Catholic Church.
The glossary requires 'schisms' for schismata, preserving the technical term for divisions in the Church.
The glossary gives 'heresies' for haereses; here the adjective 'heretical' modifies 'perversity' to describe the corrupting false teaching.
Occasus literally means 'setting' (as of the sun); rendering it as 'setting' preserves the image of the world's decline at the end of the age.

bible_refs.note: in nouissimis diebus aderunt tempora molesta ... sicut et illorum fuit

pass_b_english: But what unity does he preserve, what love does he keep or even consider, who is driven mad by the fury of discord, splits the Church, destroys faith, disturbs peace, scatters love, and profanes the sacred sign?

This evil, most faithful brothers, had begun long ago, but now the hostile disaster of that same evil has grown, and the venomous ruin of heretical perversity and schisms has begun to rise up and spring forth more and more. For so it had to be at the setting of the world, as the Holy Spirit forewarned and admonished us through the apostle: “In the last days troublesome times will come. People will be lovers of themselves, proud, puffed up, greedy, blasphemous, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, impious, without affection, without loyalty, accusers, without self-control, unkind, not loving what is good, traitors, reckless, swollen with stupor, loving pleasures more than God, holding a form of religion but denying its power. From these come those who creep into houses and prey on weak women loaded down with sins, led by various desires, always learning and never arriving at knowledge of the truth. And just as Jannes and Jambres resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth, but they will not get very far. For their folly will be plain to everyone, as theirs also was” (2 Timothy 3:1-9).

Everything that was foretold is being fulfilled, and now that the end of the age is drawing near, the testing of people and times alike has come. As the adversary rages more and more, error deceives, stupor puffs up, envy burns, greed blinds, impiety corrupts, pride inflates, discord embitters, and anger hurls people down.

problems.why: Source 'stupore' means stupor/dullness, not conceit; 'inflati' goes with conceit elsewhere but here it's 'stupor'.
problems.fix: swollen with stupor, or puffed up with dullness
problems.ruling: 'stupore inflati' means inflated with stupor/dullness, not conceit. 'Conceit' changes the vice listed.

problems.why: Source 'stupor' (stupor/dullness) is mistranslated as 'conceit'; different vices are listed.
problems.fix: stupor puffs up, or dullness exalts
problems.ruling: 'stupor extollit' means stupor exalts, not conceit. Different vice mistranslated, changing meaning.

fixed: Changed 'swollen with conceit' to 'swollen with stupor': source 'stupore inflati' means swollen with stupor/dullness, not conceit.
Changed 'conceit puffs up' to 'stupor puffs up': source 'stupor extollit' means stupor/dullness exalts, not conceit.

last_rejected.quote: as the Holy Spirit forewarned and admonished us through the apostle
last_rejected.source_quote: praenuntiante per apostolum nobis et praemonente Spiritu sancto
last_rejected.why: English reverses agency: source has Spirit speaking through apostle, not apostle speaking with Spirit's help.
last_rejected.fix: as the Holy Spirit, foretelling and warning us through the apostle
last_rejected.ruling: Ablative participles 'praenuntiante...Spiritu sancto' and 'praemonente' both modify Spirit; English correctly conveys Spirit forewarning through apostle.

last_rejected.why: Stupor in Latin means amazement/astonishment here, not modern 'stupor' (unconsciousness).
last_rejected.fix: puffed up with conceit / swollen with arrogance
last_rejected.ruling: 'Stupore inflati' renders 2 Tim 3:4 'tetuphōmenoi'; 'stupor' in ecclesiastical Latin means pride/conceit, matching 'swollen with' adequately.

last_rejected.why: Same word: stupor means conceit/arrogance, not unconsciousness; repeated error.
last_rejected.ruling: Same Latin 'stupor' in parallel construction; 'puffs up' correctly conveys inflation/arrogance sense, not unconsciousness. No real error.
